title: Admin Scripting Hub & Runbook Taskifier
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a unified Admin Scripting Hub that converts operational runbooks into first-class, idempotent task flows with a minimal CLI and HTTP API for support engineers. The hub will: 1) host vetted admin scripts (bash/py/golang wrappers) with semantic metadata (preconditions, safe mode, detectable side effects), 2) provide a 'taskifier' that turns runbook steps into discrete retryable tasks with checkpoints, 3) expose a lightweight HTTP endpoint for the Console and chat ops assistant to trigger tasks with RBAC and audit logging, and 4) integrate with existing incident tooling (PagerDuty, Slack, and our runbook library). Goals: reduce manual error, shorten mean time to resolution, and make runbook execution observable and reversible where possible.
acceptance_criteria: Admin Scripting Hub service deployed to staging with TLS and KMS-protected secrets
At least 8 canonical runbook scripts onboarded with metadata and safe-mode flags
Taskifier produces tasks that can be queued, retried, and inspected in the Tasks UI
Console can invoke a task via HTTP and receives structured run results (status, logs, artifacts)
Audit log entries created for every run with user, task id, inputs (redacted), and outputs
RBAC enforced using existing SSO groups and tested end-to-end
Automated rollback / compensating action pattern documented for risky scripts
tasks: Design schema for script metadata and precondition checks
Implement task engine (queue + checkpoint store + retries)
Add KMS integration and secrets fetch for script runtime
Build CLI wrapper to validate scripts and publish to hub
Add HTTP API endpoints for task creation, status, and cancellation
Wire audit events into existing logging pipeline and retention policy
Create 8 example runbooks from support playbooks and onboard to staging
End-to-end test: trigger high-severity db-failover script in staging (dry-run, then safe-mode)
